title: HE WAS ANGRY.
paragraphs: And that one moment of anger cost Moses the Promised Land.

Forty years of leadership pressure.
Forty years of complaints.
Forty years of people saying:
“Why did you bring us here to die?”
The crowd gathers. Voices rising. Accusations flying.
“You and Aaron brought us into this wilderness to kill us!”
Imagine the weight on Moses’ chest.
A leader carrying the thirst, fear, and rebellion of an entire nation.

Not shout.
Not strike.
Not perform.
Because the miracle wasn’t about Moses’ strength.
But anger does something dangerous to leaders.
Moses walks before the people, staff in hand, voice shaking.
“Listen, you rebels… must we bring you water from this rock?”
Then comes one of the most heartbreaking lines in Scripture.
Because you did not trust Me enough to honor Me as holy before Israel…
you will not bring this community into the land.

The man who faced Pharaoh.
The man who split the Red Sea.
The man who spoke with God face to face.
Because leadership anger can turn God’s glory into a personal performance.
And God will not share His glory.
But here is the Gospel thread hidden in the rock.
In 1 Corinthians 10:4, Paul reveals something stunning:
The rock in the wilderness was a shadow.
Jesus would be the true Rock struck for our salvation.
The rock in Numbers was struck once.
After that, it was only to be spoken to.
Because Christ would be struck once for all.
Hebrews 10:10 says Jesus’ sacrifice happened once for all time.
Maybe you’re a leader under pressure.

A parent.
A pastor.
A manager.
A servant carrying too many voices in your ear.
anger has been closer than prayer.
Your worst moment does not cancel God’s redemption.
Yes, Moses missed the Promised Land.
But in Matthew 17, something stunning happens.
On the Mount of Transfiguration, standing beside Jesus in glory…
The man who struck the rock…
Before anger swings the staff again…
And mercy is still deeper than your worst moment.
Someone you know is one moment away from striking the rock.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
